It is not blocking GT. I have also found that attribute selectors for components cause a lot of confusion and should be avoided.

e.g. We have a component `g-button[button-style=action]` and developers are confused when <g-button button-style={{expression}}></g-select> does not work. (I realize that particular syntax is deprecated in A2, but the point stands)

issue.title: Attribute as component selector not recognized
issue.body:
After updating my plunk from alpha.20 to alpha.22 I've got following exception:

``` Shell
Component 'A' can only have an element selector, but had '[a]'

Error
    at new BaseException (https://code.angularjs.org/2.0.0-alpha.22/angular2.dev.js:5938:25)
    at DirectiveParser._ensureComponentOnlyHasElementSelector (https://code.angularjs.org/2.0.0-alpha.22/angular2.dev.js:19095:21)
```

See console in plunk for detailed stack trace.

Plunk: http://plnkr.co/edit/yXqVIkJXG3OXsoouYTN2?p=preview

body:
When fixed, will it follow reasonable selector specificity rules if there are potential collisions?  For example, I would like to have a generic component for fields with a selector of `field` and more specialized components for some of them such as `field[type=boolean]`.  Given the host element `<field type="boolean">` both selectors would evaluate to true, but the second is the desired.

If selectors have to be mutually exclusive, it forces (at the very least) the more generic component to know about all the others, causing deployment of a new component to require code modifications outside of itself.  Not allowing this in order to help avoid collisions comes at the cost of extensibility (my components will have to remain open for modification).

I've switched tactics from Component selectors to using DynamicComponentLoader to try to overcome the limitations with selectors.  That however, has been running into its own set of roadblocks, such as #1236
